title: Everything in RoboDR
sub: Every capability, from reading motor commands to signed evidence, with people approving the actions that matter.

items: Decodes Unitree and ROS 2 motion, arm and hand commands
Flags unknown senders on the robot’s network, even under new identities
Spoofed, replayed or out-of-limit speed, joint and torque commands
Compares what the robot was told with what it did
Faked or frozen telemetry and disagreeing navigation sensors
Links events into attacks such as key theft or motion hijacking
Never reports “all clear” when its own inputs go silent
New processes and outbound connections on the robot
Package installs and changes to ROS 2 and robot apps
Bluetooth and Wi-Fi setup tools and wireless setting changes
Reverse tunnels, VPNs, code injection and fileless execution
Reads of the robot’s private keys and unexpected kernel modules
Attempts to change or stop RoboDR itself
Published robot attacks, including UniPwn (CVE-2025-35027)
Escalates in stages: alert, restrict, slow down, pause, safe state
Isolates the robot from the network or quarantines a rogue sender
Every motion command passed, limited or rejected
Slows the robot without changing its direction; stops never delayed
Never cuts motor power or resets the emergency stop
Each finding opens a case in AutoSecOps automatically
AI agent triages each finding and recommends a response
The AI can never delete cases, run scripts or go online
Attacker text from the robot flagged, never taken as instructions
Forged, stale or unsigned findings rejected and logged
Findings in open OCSF format for any compatible SIEM
Black box records survive power loss; any deletion shows
Auditors can verify records but cannot forge them
Every finding signed, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and tied to evidence
Pull evidence by finding or time range into the case
Whole fleet on one screen, with each robot’s cases and evidence

Add-on: signed, staged rollout of your robot apps, AI models and settings

Learns each robot’s normal, then locks it with human sign-off
Ready-made Unitree profiles; profiles pushed from the SOC need two approvers
Keys created on the robot; rotate or revoke them from the SOC
RoboDR’s own updates: signed, staged, never below your security baseline
Signed, reproducible releases with a software bill of materials (SBOM)
Starts monitor-only; protection switched on when you are ready
Two people approve safe pause, safe state and rollback

top: Reads every command to the motors
gaps: ROS 2 motion traffic is unauthenticated unless DDS security is switched on, so anyone on the network can command the robot. A sharp problem statement the page lacks.
EU Cyber Resilience Act: vulnerability reporting applies since September 2026 and all obligations from December 2027. The page cites only the Machinery Regulation.
Safety teams will ask where RoboDR stops. The deck documents its boundaries against ISO 10218, ISO 13849, IEC 60204-1 and ISO/TS 15066.
Standards documents are an engineering self-assessment, not a certification. Any IEC 62443 or CRA mention on the page should say so.
The deck has the command filter limiting dangerous commands by policy, while isolation and pauses need people. The page says every action needs approval; worth aligning.
